report.summary: Analyzed daedalus/kairos/evolution.py chunk 1 of 1: verified claims about eval timeout, import provenance, sys.executable usage, candidate scoring, and selection logic.
risks: generate_candidates | medium | No timeout on individual candidate task; a hanging manager.run_task blocks the gather indefinitely. | Add a timeout per task in the gather or per run_task call.

evaluate_candidates | medium | asyncio.gather in evaluate_candidates does not have a timeout; if evaluate_single hangs outside the subprocess (e.g., in check_import_provenance), the gather blocks forever. | Add a timeout to the gather or to evaluate_single itself.
select_best | low | Score threshold hardcoded to 100.0; if scoring changes, the selection may silently return None. | Make threshold configurable or document it as a constant.
todos: Consider adding a timeout to generate_candidates' gather.
Consider adding a timeout to evaluate_candidates' gather.
Review if score threshold in select_best should be configurable.

claims.text: Wall-clock ceiling for ONE candidate's test run. Without it a candidate that hangs blocks the whole `gather` below forever.
claims.why: The timeout is passed to asyncio.wait_for in evaluate_single, preventing indefinite hang of one candidate. However, note that the gather in evaluate_candidates itself has no timeout; the docstring refers to the per-candidate timeout, which is implemented.

claims.text: Spawns N ShadowShellManager instances in parallel to attempt the task.
claims.why: Code spawns N managers and gathers them concurrently via asyncio.gather.

claims.text: Evaluates candidates using pytest concurrently. Populates candidate.score and candidate.error.
claims.why: Code defines evaluate_single and gathers them, setting candidate.score and candidate.error.

claims.text: THE INTERPRETER IS PART OF THE MEASUREMENT. This shells out to `sys.executable -m pytest`, never to a bare `pytest`.
Bare `pytest` -> daedalus resolved to the PRIMARY checkout; `python -m pytest` -> daedalus resolved to the WORKTREE copy.
claims.why: This claim is about the behavior of the Python import system and editable installs; it cannot be verified from this code chunk alone.

claims.text: The editable install pins `daedalus` to the primary checkout by absolute path via an `_EditableFinder` on `sys.meta_path`.
claims.why: This claim describes the behavior of editable installs; not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Bare `pytest` puts only each test file's own basedir on `sys.path`, never the worktree root, so nothing shadows that finder and the candidate's edits are invisible to its own tests. `-m` puts the working directory on `sys.path[0]`, ahead of `PathFinder`, which is ahead of `_EditableFinder` -- so the candidate's code wins, as it must.
claims.why: This claim describes Python's sys.path behavior; cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: Until this changed, every score this class produced described the primary checkout's code running the candidate's tests.
claims.why: Historical claim; cannot be verified from current code.

claims.text: This is still a BINARY, whole-suite signal and it is still not a promotion boundary -- see `docs/adrs/015-ariadne-preconditions.md`.
claims.why: References an external document; cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: The stronger measurement (`daedalus.eval.correctness.evaluate_change`, which freezes the selection before candidate code runs and reports five outcomes with precedence) is the intended replacement; this fix makes the interim signal describe the right tree, nothing more.
claims.why: References external code; cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: VERIFY the docstring's argument instead of trusting it. `-m` plus this cwd makes the candidate win by sys.path ORDERING, and nothing enforced that ordering still holds -- a set PYTHONPATH, a candidate whose daedalus/ was destroyed, or a future 'simplification' back to bare `pytest` all produce the same worst-shaped failure: tests pass, score is high, wrong tree. See daedalus.eval.provenance.
claims.why: Code calls check_import_provenance(candidate.worktree_path) and voids evaluation if it fails, enforcing the docstring's concern.

claims.text: A failure here VOIDS THE EVALUATION and is not a candidate score. -1.0 is this module's own 'not evaluated' marker (used above for an incomplete candidate); 0.0 would mean 'measured, and bad', which would let an unrunnable evaluation argue against a candidate nobody actually judged.
claims.why: Code sets candidate.score = -1.0 and candidate.error = prov.as_error() when provenance check fails, consistent with the claim.

claims.text: A hung candidate is a FAILED candidate, never an unscored one left to block the gather. Kill it and say why.
claims.why: On TimeoutError, candidate.score is set to 0.0, error is set, and process is killed.

claims.text: Selects the best candidate based on the score.
claims.why: Code filters candidates by score >= 100.0, sorts descending, and returns the first.

observations.what: generate_candidates does not apply a timeout to the individual manager.run_task calls; a hanging manager blocks the gather indefinitely.
evaluate_candidates uses asyncio.gather without a timeout; if evaluate_single hangs outside the subprocess (e.g., in check_import_provenance), the gather blocks forever.
select_best uses hardcoded threshold 100.0; if scoring changes, selection may silently return None.
